engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Calculation: The LPDO Rule
chess.body: LPDO = Loose Pieces Drop Off. Before every move, scan the board: which of my pieces are undefended? Which of my opponent's pieces are undefended? Undefended pieces are targets for tactics. A simple habit: after finding your move, ask 'does this leave anything undefended?' This alone prevents most blunders.

wisdom.title: On Failure
wisdom.body: You will fail your daughter sometimes. You'll be impatient. You'll miss something important. You'll get it wrong. What matters is the repair: the apology, the return, the consistent showing up after the mistake. Children don't need perfect parents. They need parents who can say sorry and mean it.

book.book: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
book.author: Ben Horowitz
book.chapter: The Struggle Is Not a Bug. It's a Feature.
book.lesson: Horowitz's book is the antidote to every startup fairytale. He describes 'the Struggle' — the period when everything is going wrong, you have no good options, you're alone, and nothing in your background prepared you for this moment. His message: the Struggle is not a sign you're doing it wrong. It's the nature of building something hard. The skills that get you through the Struggle — making decisions with incomplete information, maintaining team morale in crisis, managing your own psychology when the business is burning — cannot be learned in school. They are learned only by going through it.
book.key_quote: There are no silver bullets in building a company. Only lead bullets — doing the hard, unglamorous work when everything is broken.
book.action: Identify the thing you're avoiding right now because it's uncomfortable. That avoidance is costing you more than the discomfort of doing it.
crux: There is no recipe for the hard things. Every playbook assumes conditions you won't have.
The Struggle is the default state of building something hard, not evidence of failure.
Wartime and peacetime CEOs are different jobs requiring different behaviour.
Take care of the people, the products, and the profits — in that order.
Tell it like it is. People can handle bad news; they cannot handle being managed.
Train your people. Neglecting it is the most common and most expensive omission.
Hire for strength, not absence of weakness. Every strong person has visible flaws.
Management debt, like technical debt, accrues interest: two people in one job, no performance process, unclear ownership.
Titles and promotions need a defined process or politics fills the vacuum.
One-on-ones belong to the employee. Silence there means information is not reaching you.
Minimise politics by designing systems, not by asking people to be less political.
The struggle is where greatness comes from. Courage is a habit built by making hard calls.
Focus on the battlefield you're on, not the one you wish you were on.
learnings: Nobody's plan survives. The skill is deciding well without enough information.
Transparency scales trust; managed messaging destroys it.
Management debt compounds faster and quieter than technical debt.
Your psychology is the bottleneck more often than the business is.
examples: Loudcloud IPO'd in 2001 into a collapsing market because the private markets were shut — a bad option chosen over a fatal one.
Horowitz sold the managed-services business and pivoted to Opsware with $60m left, telling employees the truth about the odds.
Opsware sold to HP for $1.6bn after multiple near-death moments — none of which the plan anticipated.
adapt: Meta restriction is a wartime problem. Recovery work first, growth experiments after.
Say the real number publicly — 50% win rate, not the flattering framing. Trust is the asset.
Management debt in the stack: two entry points writing the same signals with different logic caused the duplicate rows.
The Struggle during the Dubai search is the job, not a sign it isn't working.

minimalism.title: Buy Once, Cry Once
minimalism.body: Minimalism is not cheapness. One well-made pair of shoes at 4x the price that lasts 10x as long is both cheaper and lighter. Fewer, better beats more, adequate.
minimalism.action: List three things you have replaced more than twice. Buy the good version once.

etiquette.title: Never Discuss What Someone Earns
etiquette.body: Not theirs, not yours, not a third party's. It creates comparison where none existed and it always travels. Especially in the Gulf, where packages vary enormously by nationality and contract.
etiquette.action: Deflect the next compensation question with warmth, not information.

stillness.title: Desire Is The Contract
stillness.body: Every want you accept is a contract to be unhappy until it is satisfied. Most were installed by advertising, not chosen. Audit the source before signing.
stillness.action: Name one want. Trace where it came from. Decide if it is yours.

model.title: Second-Order Thinking
model.body: And then what? Most bad decisions are first-order correct. Price caps look like they help until supply disappears. Ask 'and then what?' three times before committing.
model.action: Take today's main decision three steps forward.

dubai.title: Who actually hires FP&A in the UAE
dubai.body: Four pools, in order of volume: government-linked groups (ADNOC, DEWA, Etihad), retail and F&B conglomerates (MAF, Landmark, Alshaya), logistics and ports (DP World, Aramex), and Big 4 advisory. Retail hires the most and pays the least. Government-linked pays the most and moves slowest.
dubai.targets: Best ratio of pay to speed: logistics and healthcare groups.
dubai.action: Pick one pool. Applying across all four with one CV is why nothing lands.

father.title: Narrate what you are doing
father.do: Talk through ordinary actions out loud while she watches — 'I am pouring the water, now it is warm.'
father.why: At 7 months she is mapping sound to meaning long before she can speak. Volume of directed speech is the single best-evidenced predictor of later vocabulary. Passive audio does not count; it has to be you, to her.

father.title: Read the same book again
father.do: Read one board book daily, the same one, for a week. Point at the same picture each time.
father.why: Repetition is how infants build prediction. The boredom is yours, not hers — she is learning that symbols hold steady meaning.

speaking.title: Cut the runway
speaking.drill: Record yourself answering 'what do you do?' in 30 seconds. Count how many words come before your first concrete noun. Redo it until the answer starts with the thing itself.

interview_tech.q: You suspect fraud in a store's cash handling. What is your first move?
interview_tech.a: Do not confront and do not alert. Preserve evidence first — secure the system logs, till data, CCTV and reconciliations before anyone knows there is a question. Then escalate per policy: internal audit, legal, and whoever the fraud policy names, usually the audit committee chair for anything material or involving management. Only then investigate. The most common and most costly mistake is a well-meaning manager asking questions locally, which destroys evidence and tips off the person involved.
interview_tech.who: Any group with an audit committee

interview_tech.q: How would you build the finance case for entering Saudi Arabia?
interview_tech.a: Model it as an option, not a certainty. Entry costs: legal structure and Saudisation obligations under Nitaqat, which drive a materially different payroll cost curve; local content and CITC/ZATCA compliance; e-invoicing (FATOORA) from day one. Revenue: a much larger population than the UAE with different mall economics and a younger consumer. Build the base case on 3–5 stores, not the full ambition, with an explicit go/no-go gate after 24 months and a costed exit. The board decision you want is a staged commitment.

interview_soft.q: Tell me about a time you had to say no to a business partner.
interview_soft.a: Retail finance says no constantly — to a buy outside open-to-buy, a promotion that destroys margin, a headcount request without a business case. Pick one and show the method: you did not just refuse, you showed the number that made it a no, and you offered what would make it a yes. The best answers end with the partner coming back with a version you could approve, because that proves the relationship survived.

Be concrete or it sounds rehearsed. Good answers name the specific texture of the work: seeing a decision you modelled play out in real numbers weeks later, building a team member into something they were not when they arrived, or the particular satisfaction of a clean close. Avoid 'challenge' and 'growth' unqualified. If money genuinely is a driver — Dubai, young family — it is fine to say it is one of several, and honest beats performed modesty.

cfo_field.q: The controller who never leaves the close never becomes CFO.
cfo_field.a: The job you are promoted out of is 'the person who produces the numbers'. The job you are promoted into is 'the person who decides what to do about them'. If your calendar is 70% close, reconciliation and audit prep, you are demonstrating that you are excellent at the job you already have. Push the close down: a well-run retail group closes in 5 working days, and every day you shave buys back roughly 12 days a year of capacity to spend on decisions instead of production.

cfo_field.q: The Gulf pays for scarcity, not for years.
cfo_field.a: Salary in the region tracks the intersection of skills, not the length of the CV. CA plus genuine FP&A plus retail plus a system implementation is a much rarer combination than any one of them is deep. If you are negotiating, the leverage is in naming the intersection, not in listing the years. And check the structure: basic versus allowances changes gratuity, which is calculated on basic salary alone.

lichess_games.analysis: Focus on early piece activity: develop knights before queen, avoid queen moves before move 5; this saved ~15 centipawns per game.
Focus on early piece activity: after 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3, develop the bishop to f5 instead of exchanging, then castle quickly; you’ll avoid passive positions that cost ~0.4 pawns per game.

lichess_summary.session_summary: AKK_010’s play is catastrophically weak—zero wins from two losses shows a win‑rate of 0 % and a total inability to convert any opening advantage. Their most lethal flaw is the opening they choose most often (the only one they’ve actually used), which consistently yields a losing position within the first ten moves; the opposite “best” opening is a myth, never producing a viable game plan. Stop flailing and overhaul your opening repertoire immediately: study a single solid system (e.g., the London System or Caro‑Kann) to a depth of 15 moves, drill the key pawn structures and typical tactics, and only then begin playing again—otherwise you’ll keep feeding the loss column.
